story_type: Black Hawk bucket drops on a forest fire, smoke wall, pass after pass
hook: Six hundred sixty gallons, dropped on a forest fire in one pass.
narration: Six hundred sixty gallons of water, dropped on a forest fire in a single pass.
In July 2012, wildfires were burning across Arkansas, and the state forestry commission needed help.
Early on the Fourth of July, the Army National Guard staged two UH-60 Black Hawks in Hot Springs.
Each one flew with a bucket hanging on a long line below it.
The bucket opens at the bottom when the pilot hits a release, and the whole load falls at once.
The crews flew back and forth along the smoke, pass after pass.
Some runs went straight over the fire line, into the edge of the plume.
From the cabin, the crew watched the bucket swing out over the burning pines.
outcome: By then the Guard crews had flown seventy missions and dropped over fifty thousand gallons on fires in five counties.
title: Black Hawks bomb an Arkansas wildfire
description:
Arkansas Army National Guard UH-60 Black Hawk crews drop water on wildfires for the Arkansas Forestry Commission in July 2012, 660 gallons in each pass.
